Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings and impressions from transcript and DDx: Acute/subacute (~1 week) fluid-like swelling at left olecranon tip; slightly warm; minimal tenderness; full range of motion preserved; no systemic symptoms. Clinician impression: likely olecranon bursitis (non-septic). DDx supports aseptic olecranon bursitis as most likely.  
- Differential diagnoses from DDx consistent with transcript:  
  - Aseptic (non-septic) olecranon bursitis — Likelihood: High. Justification: localized fluid-like swelling at elbow tip, slight warmth, preserved motion, clinician directly suspected bursitis.  
  - Septic olecranon bursitis / localized cellulitis — Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: local warmth could indicate infection; opposing evidence: no fever, minimal pain, no spreading erythema; clinician judged septic arthritis unlikely.  
  - Gout-related bursitis / crystal arthropathy — Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: acute localized inflammatory presentation and clinician planned gout testing; opposing evidence: patient reports minimal pain and no prior gout history.  
- Working diagnosis and management priorities: Working diagnosis — likely aseptic olecranon bursitis. Priorities: reduce inflammation/pain, exclude infectious or rheumatologic/metabolic causes via blood tests, monitor for signs of infection requiring urgent review.

Management Plan

- Immediate actions and treatments: Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food (patient advised to stop if heartburn occurs). Duration not documented. Patient advised this is OTC and to take with food.  
- Investigations arranged: Blood tests to include inflammatory markers, infection screening, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout evaluation; blood test forms to be mailed to patient.  
- Follow-up and monitoring: Arrange follow-up after blood tests (phone/video or face-to-face per patient preference). Patient instructed to contact promptly for urgent review if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, redness spreads, or systemic symptoms develop (emergency concern).  
- Patient education: Reassured that presentation is unlikely life‑threatening; explained warning signs of septic process and when to seek urgent care. Advised to report worsening symptoms and to complete blood testing.  
- Referrals: No specialist or allied health referrals documented at this visit.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Aseptic (non-septic) olecranon bursitis — High likelihood. Rationale: localized fluid-filled swelling at olecranon tip, slight warmth, preserved ROM, clinician identified bursitis.  
- Septic olecranon bursitis / localized cellulitis — Moderate likelihood. Rationale: local warmth could represent infection; however, lack of systemic signs and minimal pain reduce immediate probability. Monitor for worsening/redness/fever.  
- Gout-related bursitis / crystal arthropathy — Moderate likelihood. Rationale: acute inflammatory swelling can be crystal-mediated; clinician ordered gout screening. Less likely given minimal pain and no gout history.
